newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Bildt warns against complacency in Yugoslavia.
newsitem.headline: Bildt warns against complacency in Yugoslavia.

text.p: International mediator Carl Bildt warned the West on Thursday to guard against complacency in Bosnia, saying a fragile peace could end in the blink of an eye.
"There is no self-sustaining peace," said Bildt, the international community's envoy to Bosnia. "If we left today it would fall apart tomorrow."

Bildt, speaking to reporters after a meeting of the Bosnian Peace Implementation Steering Committee, said however that he was cautiously optimistic the hard-fought peace could be sustained with political, military and economic willpower.
Bildt said authorities in the Moslem-Croat Bosnian Federation were making slow, sometimes tedious, progress towards establishing a more normal society, but at least it was progress.

"Every milimetre forward is as the result of intense discussion," he said. "Sometimes we go forwards two milimetres, sometimes we go backwards by one ... but at least the general direction is the right one.
Bildt said every gesture -- even the adoption of a bi-national flag, coat-of-arms and seal -- helped towards reconciliation.
But he stressed the need for pressure to be brought for the speed establishment of so-called "common institutions" such as a central bank and constitutional court.

Bosnia's citizens voted on September 14 for joint governing institutions to reunite a country split by war into ethnic fiefs. But efforts to establish the complex ruling structure have been slowed by nationalist feuding and manoeuvring.
Bildt said he hoped the West could also speedily agree to the make-up of the peace-keeping force currently under discussion.
He said he favoured a local force "with the power of deterrence", but refused to be drawn on its size.
